newsitem.title: FRANCE: British Telecom starts business services in France.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom starts business services in France.

text.p: British Telecom Plc on Tuesday announced the opening of a national telecoms service for companies in the Lyon region, making use of the increasing liberalisation of the French telecommunication sector.

The system unveiled by British Telecom France, called "Pleiade", is an alternative to the public service offered by France Telecom for the long distance calls within France and is in addition to the international services already offered by BT to French businesses.
France Telecom will be partially privatised in the spring of 1997 and the French telecommunications sector is gradually being opened up towards full liberalisation in 1998.

"Our objective is to become the second operator in each European country by obtaining in the next five to seven years a share of between five and 10 percent of the market," said Pierre-Henri Drevon, managing director of BT France.
"France Telecom will keep a 80 percent stake but the market will increase by 50 percent. There is place for alternatives," he said.
British Telecom is not the only one aiming to become the second-biggest operator in France.

Generale des Eaux, already active in mobile telecommunications with its SFR unit, earlier this month announced the creation of a special unit, called Cegetel, which also strives to become number two in France.
Generale des Eaux, a diversified conglomerate, has links with Southwestern Bell, Vodafone as well as AT&T and is looking for a German partner. Analysts see Mannesmann and VEBA as possible allies.
British Telecom, the first telecoms operator to be privatised in Europe, will launch Pleiade before the end of the year also in Lille, Marseille and Paris.

Main rivals will be the Siris joint-venture of Generale des Eaux and Unisource, as well as MFS World Com of the U.S. and the alliance of France Telecom with Germany's Deutsche Telekom and Sprint Corp of the U.S.
There have been rumours in French newspapers about BT being in talks with Generale des Eaux to replace AT&T in the Siris structure with its own BT/MCI transatlantic system.

BT has no comment on this rumour, which would be in conflict with merger talks between AT&T's European operations and Unisource -- a venture of Dutch Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV, Swiss Telecom, Telia of Sweden and Telefonica de Espana SA of Spain.
BT France said that "Pleiade" would offer telecommunications cost cuts of 25 percent on national calls and 40 percent on international calls.
France Telecom has recently slashed its long distance national rates in a bid to fend off the competition.
